standard_prerequisites.name: A local complete intersection homomorphism presents the target as a quotient of a polynomial algebra by a Koszul ideal
The ring map is perfect iff the ideal is perfect as a module, by the perfect ring-map and perfect module lemmas
Perfectness of a module is local, by the glueing lemma
Locally a Koszul ideal is generated by a Koszul-regular sequence, which admits a finite free resolution

core_obligations: Unfold the definition: A -> B is a local complete intersection homomorphism means B = A[x_1, ..., x_n]/I with I a Koszul ideal (proof lines 21857-21860).
Reduce: by the perfect ring-map lemma and the perfect module lemma it suffices to prove I is a perfect module over A[x_1, ..., x_n] (proof lines 21861-21862).

Localize: by the glueing lemma perfectness is local, so assume I is generated by a Koszul-regular sequence per the regular-ideal definition; such an ideal has a finite free resolution, proving I perfect and hence A -> B perfect (proof lines 21863-21866).
proof_roadmap: Unfold the lci definition to a Koszul ideal presentation (proof lines 21857-21860).
Reduce to perfectness of the ideal (proof lines 21861-21862).
Localize and conclude via the Koszul-regular finite free resolution (proof lines 21863-21866).
